title: A Hundred Lockers
statement: $100$ closed lockers stand in a row. Student $k$ (for $k = 1,\dots,100$) toggles every locker whose number is a multiple of $k$. How many lockers are open at the end?
insight: Locker n is toggled once per divisor; divisors pair up as d and n/d except when n is a perfect square.
redHerring: Simulating the first few students looking for a pattern.
hints: A locker ends open iff it has an odd number of divisors.
Pair each divisor $d$ with $n/d$. When does this fail?
solution: Locker $n$ is toggled once per divisor of $n$. Divisors pair as $(d, n/d)$, except that $d=\sqrt n$ pairs with itself. So $n$ has an odd number of divisors iff it is a perfect square. The open lockers are $1,4,9,\dots,100$: $10$ of them.
